answer: An agent forecasting walnut yields in a garden over a seasonal horizon combines advisers using multiplicative weights. A vetted adviser starts with a fixed weight; registering child accounts divides that weight instead of creating new weight. After each observed harvest, every weight is multiplied by exp(-loss) using the same scoring rule. Identical forecasts from clones therefore retain exactly the combined influence of one adviser, not extra votes. This blocks clone amplification if root admission is controlled; diverse forecasts remain a different attack.
